title: A table whose column has no lineage filters nothing as a CALCULATE filter
query: VAR Blue = SELECTCOLUMNS ( FILTER ( VALUES ( Product[Color] ), Product[Color] = "Blue" ), "c", Product[Color] & "" )

source.quote: it returns the same value as Sales Amount without applying any filter
source.supports: the article's v3 measure: a filter table column that has no lineage of a model column applies no filter

source.quote: adding an empty string to Product[Category] in the previous expression does not change the column content, whereas it does break the data lineage

derivation: The variable holds one row, "Blue", in a column computed by an expression: no lineage. Used as a filter it restricts no model column, so the measure is the total, 540. With lineage it would be 80.
alternative: If the engine rejects a filter table whose only column has no lineage, the query is an error. If it kept the lineage through the concatenation, the result would be 80.
notes: The article's example has one column with lineage beside the one without; here the table has only the column without lineage.
